title: TE Don Clements v. Blue Ridge Presbytery — Decision on Request for Reference
disposition_detail: The SJC denied Blue Ridge Presbytery’s request to refer the complaint and directed Presbytery to hear and decide it. The underlying complaint’s merits were not decided.
first_summary: Blue Ridge Presbytery asked the SJC to hear and decide a complaint by reference. The SJC denied the request because the record showed neither presbytery-wide disqualification nor serious division, constitutional questions, or unusually difficult issues warranting reference. Presbytery was directed to hear and decide the complaint.
summary: Blue Ridge Presbytery asked the SJC to hear and decide a complaint by reference. The SJC denied the request because the record demonstrated neither presbytery-wide disqualification nor serious division, constitutional questions, or new, delicate, or difficult issues warranting reference. Presbytery therefore had to hear and decide the complaint itself. The ruling concerned only the proper court for adjudication and did not decide the complaint’s merits; companion case 2017-07 was answered by reference to this decision.

sources.supports: Case identity, request for reference, reasons for denial, direction to Presbytery, companion-case treatment, and unanimous approval.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 11–13 identify cases 2017-06/2017-07 and the SJC decisions; lines 29–31 record unanimous SJC approval.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 15–16 state that Blue Ridge Presbytery requested a BCO 41-3 reference so the SJC could hear and decide the complaint.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 17–25 find no demonstrated bias, universal disqualification, serious division, constitutional question, or sufficiently difficult issue; the reference was denied and Presbytery ordered to decide the complaint.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The decision does not adjudicate the underlying complaint’s merits. Lines 29–31 show unanimity.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Line 27 says companion complaint 2017-07 was answered by reference to the decision in 2017-06; case 2017-06 itself incorporates no separate decision.

source_limits: The short combined decision does not describe the complaint’s substantive allegations or decide their merits.
